headline: OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion as AI spending growth stalls
dek: OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion while Ramp data shows AI spending stalling, Google takes over a troubled data centre project, Meta's Muse builds custom spaces and Amazon lets you text Alexa to shop[S1][S2][S3][S6][S8].
what_happened: OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion after raising another $11 billion, Bloomberg reports, while Ramp data shows AI spending flattening[S1][S2].
Crusoe sold an unfinished Wyoming data centre project to Google, which plans to invest $17 billion in it[S3].
Meta's Muse agents can now build custom spaces, like trackers and planners, from a description in chat[S5][S6].

sections.title: OpenAI hits a $1.25 trillion valuation as AI spending growth stalls
paragraphs: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg, The Verge reports[S2]. That comes not long after OpenAI raised $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion[S2]. Bloomberg says OpenAI is still pursuing more investment that could take the round to $20 billion, after it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation[S2].

At the same time, a new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose[S1]. According to Ramp's data, token spend grew only 1.5% across August and September, after growing 42% in July from the previous month[S1]. October did see a re-acceleration, with token spend up 8.9% from September 23 to October 23[S1].

Ramp's lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch that almost all AI spending comes from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies[S1]. He said the slowdown is not a demand problem and pointed instead to competition: in September, OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna[S1]. OpenAI's rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week, The Verge reports[S2].

card.hook: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reports[S2].
points: The new round raised another $11 billion and could reach $20 billion[S2].
Ramp says AI token spend grew just 1.5% across August and September[S1].
In July, that spending had grown 42% from the month before[S1].
card.take: Cheaper AI prices may be capping how fast AI companies grow[S1].
card.ask: Is the AI money boom slowing down[S2][S1]?

sections.title: Google takes over a troubled Wyoming data centre as OpenAI drops NDAs
paragraphs: Crusoe, a Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google[S3]. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline[S3]. Google did not disclose how much it paid, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus[S3].

Crusoe first announced the project last year with infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity[S3]. TechCrunch says The deal shows how hard it can be for independent developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power[S3]. Crusoe is still developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas[S3].

Separately, OpenAI announced that it won't use non-disclosure agreements with public officials on its data center projects, after midterm voters voiced their opposition to data center expansion, The Verge reports[S4]. OpenAI says it will pay the full cost of the electricity it uses and of the infrastructure needed to serve it[S4]. In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies on data center projects[S4].

sections.title: Meta's Muse agents can now build custom spaces
paragraphs: Meta has launched Spaces, a new way to work with its Muse AI agents, TechCrunch reports[S5]. Meta says Users can describe an idea in chat and Muse builds a space, such as a tracker, a planner or a project board[S5]. The Verge reports examples like a shopping hub, a school dashboard, a music tracker and a trivia game[S6].

If users connect outside apps such as Gmail, Google Calendar, OpenTable or Notion, Muse keeps pulling information from them to update prices, dates and other details in the background[S6]. Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's founder and CEO, posted on X that he had made a BBQ game, an event tracker and a home control dashboard with spaces[S5].

Spaces is the second new Muse feature in a week: on Thursday, Meta made Muse Voice, which lets users video chat with their agent, available to everyone in the US[S5][S7]. During its earnings call in October, Zuckerberg said Meta's agents had 10 million users in the US and Canada, less than two months after they debuted[S5].

sections.title: Amazon now lets you text Alexa to shop
paragraphs: Amazon is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, TechCrunch reports[S8]. Select US customers will Get a text asking them to turn on the feature, and others can join a waitlist as it rolls out more broadly in the coming weeks[S8]. The Verge reports that Users can describe a product or send a photo, and Alexa for Shopping will search Amazon listings, text back recommendations and order the item for them[S9].

The text agent can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products and check the status of orders[S8]. Amazon says Alexa will learn users' preferences over time and suggest items accordingly[S8]. The contact appears in a user's phone as Amazon Alexa[S9].

The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta's Muse from querying its site in September, and just before the start of the holiday shopping season[S8]. TechCrunch notes that Last month DoorDash said third-party agents had placed only hundreds of orders in total on its platform, and that it plans to focus on its own text-based agent[S8].

why_it_matters.text: The AI race is getting richer and cheaper at the same time: OpenAI's value keeps climbing while Ramp sees spending growth slow as prices fall[S1][S2]. If the price war continues, users win, and AI companies may grow more slowly than investors expect[S1].

Data centres are now a public issue: after the midterms, OpenAI is promising more openness and to pay its own power costs[S4]. Google's takeover in Wyoming shows how hard these huge builds can be[S3].
